title: Transitive normalized costalk cohomology transitions
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, and let $T$ be a Noetherian excellent scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use $D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, geometric costalks $C_zM=R\Gamma_zM$, roots-of-unity twists, and the fixed codimension-one residue normalization of [def-per-potential-dualizing]. For each geometric specialization $v\rightsquigarrow w$ of codimension $c$ (the dimension of the reduced closure of $v$ in $T_{(w)}$) and every $M\in D^+(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ there are natural maps
$$\operatorname{sp}^{i}_{v,w}:H^i(C_vM)\longrightarrow H^{i+2c}(C_wM(c))\qquad(i\in\mathbf Z).$$
They agree with the fixed residue transition for $c=1$, and with transport along the geometric specialization for $c=0$. They are compatible with twists and with composition of geometric specializations, adding the codimensions; equivalently, composition along a chain of immediate specializations is independent of that factorization. Every positive-codimension geometric specialization has such a finite immediate factorization. The maps commute with open restriction and localization, including strict localization. If $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], the supported-composition identifications $C_z(i^!M)\cong C_zM$ for $z\in Z$ identify the transition maps on $Z$ with those on $T$ for specializations in $Z$. Here $i^!$ is the supported derived inverse image specified in [def-per-potential-dualizing].

source.place: Expose XVII, Theorem 3.1.2, Section 3.5 (independence of factorization), and Proposition 3.5.4 for closed immersions as finite morphisms; localization and strict-local conventions of Sections 1 and 3.5.

proof.text: Identify the coefficient case $n=1$, $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z=\mathbf F_\ell$, in [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex] with [def-per-potential-dualizing]. These definitions use the same residue-field supported kernel, its geometric fibre, the same sheaf $\mu_\ell$ and its tensor/dual powers, and the same normalized immediate map: restrict to the strict localization, take the reduced one-dimensional closure, apply $\nu^*i^!$, and multiply its trait map by $d^{-1}$. In both trait formulas the map is wild averaging followed by evaluation at $\sigma$ and inverse evaluation at $1-\sigma$. Thus specializing the prime-power conventions to $n=1$ changes neither the costalks nor the residue normalization. No potentiality or choice of pinnings is used.

source.place: XVII Sections 1.2–1.4; comparison of the two coefficient conventions at n=1

proof.text: For positive codimension, apply [lem-per-normal-top-residue-class] with $n=1$. Its canonical maps are natural in $M$, agree with the normalized immediate transitions, and compose with the indicated twists and degree shifts. For codimension zero define the map by transport of the geometric fibre of $R\Gamma_tM$ along the specified geometric specialization; this is functorial and is the identity only for the identity specialization. By Step 7, every positive-codimension geometric specialization is a composite of finitely many immediate geometric specializations; codimension-zero transports may also be inserted. If the successive codimensions are $e_j\in\{0,1\}$ and $b_j=\sum_{k<j}e_k$, the $j$th factor is the immediate transition for $M(b_j)$ in degree $i+2b_j$, with target $H^{i+2b_{j+1}}(C_{x_{j+1}}M(b_{j+1}))$. The composition clause of [lem-per-normal-top-residue-class] composes maps with these indicated degrees and twists into the map of the composite arrow, so $b_r=c$ and the composite has target $H^{i+2c}(C_wM(c))$, and the composition clause of the cited general-transition theorem gives independence of the factorization and naturality for every integer $i$.

Check twist compatibility on an immediate factor. By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], the sheaf $\Lambda(a)$, for any integer $a$, is a locally free line, commutes with inverse image and has compatible tensor/evaluation identifications. On the strictly henselian trait of [lem-per-codimension-one-costalk-reduction], choose a generator $e$ of this line, thereby identifying $L(a)$ with $L\otimes_\Lambda\Lambda e$. In the model of [lem-per-trait-residue-model], averaging sends $m\otimes e$ to $\operatorname{av}_S(m)\otimes e$, and evaluation at $\sigma$ and at $1-\sigma$ sends a functional tensored with $e$ to its value tensored with $e$. Thus the cochain map for $L(a)$ is $s_\sigma(L)\otimes 1$; totalization gives the same equality for complexes. The reduction's costalk identifications respect twists, and multiplication by $d^{-1}$ is scalar, so the equality holds for the normalized immediate map. A different generator is $ue$, and both sides are multiplied by the same unit $u$, so this equality is independent of the choice. Transport also commutes with tensor and dual powers. Apply this equality to each factor of Step 2 to obtain twist compatibility in every codimension.

source.place: XVII Sections 1.2.2–1.4 and Definition 3.5.1; linearity of the displayed trait model

proof.text: For open, ordinary-local and strict-local restriction, use [lem-per-normal-top-residue-class] at $n=1$ for compatibility of its positive-codimension transitions with etale and strict-local restriction and for composition. These are the maps of Step 2: they agree with the fixed immediate residues and compose, so their values on a chosen immediate factorization coincide factor by factor. Codimension-zero restriction is functoriality of the transport defined in Step 2. This uses none of the theorem's assertions about top classes. The localized scheme is again Noetherian and excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] (finite-type algebra $A$, multiplicative set $A\setminus\mathfrak p$), with $\ell$ invertible, so the transitions exist on it. Ordinary localization introduces no further transition: on an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the special point with prime $\mathfrak p$, the local ring at a retained prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq\mathfrak p$ in $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is canonically $A_{\mathfrak q}$. Its strict localization is consequently the same strict localization as before. The costalk interpretation in [lem-per-codimension-one-costalk-reduction] therefore computes both sides on the same pointed strict-local scheme with the same restricted complex. Since the immediate construction is performed there, its residue degree and trait cochain map are identical. Taking the composite proves the localization assertion. In codimension zero these statements are simply functoriality of transport; no identification of an arbitrary Galois transport with the identity is made.

source.place: XVII Definition 1.4.1, Remark 1.4.2, Theorem 3.1.2 and Section 3.5

proof.text: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be the closed immersion in the statement. Its affine rings are quotients of excellent rings, hence excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], applied to the finite-type quotient algebra and the multiplicative set $\{1\}$. In particular $Z$ is Noetherian, and $\ell$ remains invertible. By [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian], $Z_{(w)}=Z\times_TT_{(w)}$. The reduced closure of a point $v$ of $Z_{(w)}$ is therefore the same reduced closed subscheme whether taken in $Z_{(w)}$ or in $T_{(w)}$: on an affine chart, a prime containing the defining ideal has the same quotient ring in both. Thus a geometric specialization in $Z$ has the same codimension in $T$, and a finite immediate factorization in $Z$ is also such a factorization in $T$.

source.place: XVII Definitions 1.4.1 and 3.5.1; Stacks 07QU lemma-finite-type-over-excellent and 05WS lemma-quotient-strict-henselization

proof.text:
Write $\alpha_z:C_z(i^!M)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_zM$ for the natural supported-composition identifications of [lem-per-exceptional-costalk-calculus]. For each immediate arrow $x_j\rightsquigarrow x_{j+1}$ in a factorization in $Z$, that lemma states exactly that these identifications carry its normalized residue to the one in $T$. With $b_j=j$ for an all-immediate chain, on degree $i+2j$ the equality is
$$\alpha_{x_{j+1}}(j+1)\,\operatorname{sp}^{Z}_{x_j,x_{j+1}}(i^!M(j))=\operatorname{sp}^{T}_{x_j,x_{j+1}}(M(j))\,\alpha_{x_j}(j).$$
The same equality for inserted codimension-zero arrows is naturality of the geometric-fibre identifications. Compose the equations: each intermediate $\alpha_{x_j}(j)^{-1}\alpha_{x_j}(j)$ cancels, leaving
$$H^{i+2c}(\alpha_w(c))\,\operatorname{sp}^{Z,i}_{v,w}(i^!M)=\operatorname{sp}^{T,i}_{v,w}(M)\,H^i(\alpha_v).$$
Twist identifications here are those checked in Step 3. By [lem-per-normal-top-residue-class], the chosen positive-codimension composites are the general transitions on both schemes and do not depend on the factorization; codimension-zero factors are the functorial transports from Step 2. This proves the closed-immersion assertion in every codimension.

source.place: XVII Definition 1.4.1, Remark 1.4.2 and Proposition 3.5.4 (closed-immersion case)

proof.text: Existence of immediate factorizations; this step uses none of Steps 2-6. Let $\varphi:T_{(\bar y)}\to S=T_{(\bar x)}$ be a geometric specialization of codimension $c$, $y'$ the image of the closed point and $Z$ its reduced closure, so $\dim Z=c$, finite as $S$ is Noetherian local [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian]. For $c=1$ the arrow is immediate; let $c\ge2$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples] the ring of a strict localization of $T$ is a filtered colimit of etale algebras over an affine chart, so [lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit] shows that a $T$-map from $T_{(\bar y)}$ into it exists and is unique for a given image of the closed point and residue embedding into $\kappa(\bar y)$. In a chain $Z=Z_0\supsetneq\cdots\supsetneq Z_c$ of irreducible closed subsets, $Z_{c-1}=\overline{\{t\}}$ has dimension $1$: a longer chain inside it would lengthen the chain in $Z$. Choose a geometric point $a$ of $S$ over $t$ and put $\bar t=\rho a$. By [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance], $S_{(a)}\cong T_{(\bar t)}$ over $T$, so the structural map $\chi:T_{(\bar t)}\to S$ is a specialization sending the closed point to $t$; it is immediate. By [lem-per-strict-localization-discrete-fibres] some $\tilde u\in S_{(a)}$ lies over $y'$; its residue field, a colimit of finite separable extensions of $\kappa(y')$, embeds into $\kappa(\bar y)$ over the embedding given by $\varphi$. This gives a $T$-map $\psi:T_{(\bar y)}\to T_{(\bar t)}$ with closed-point image $\tilde u$; $\chi\psi$ and $\varphi$ have the same closed-point image and residue map, so $\chi\psi=\varphi$. The reduced closure of $\tilde u$ lies in $S_{(a)}\times_SZ=Z_{(a)}$ [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian], of dimension $\dim\mathcal O_{Z,t}\le c-1$ [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dimension], and is at least $1$ since $\tilde u$ lies over $y'\ne t$. Induction on $c$ factors $\psi$; append $\chi$.

Step 2 now cites Step 7, and the catenary citation is dropped. Fault 2 (minor): Step 4 now cites excellence of the localization. The five new tool uses are generic strict-henselization lemmas and are declared.
